Perplexity

Research briefs with inspectable sources.

POfficial product ↗Open in the hierarchy →
Level 4Inspect the detail

Use Perplexity's supported search and answer APIs to prepare source-linked research for a business decision. MoreSpace can build competitor monitoring briefs, market discovery workspaces, and research-assisted content planning. We preserve the original links and retrieval context, then ask an analyst to verify material claims and distinguish evidence from proposed actions before the brief is shared.

Useful outputs

  • Research draft with source links
  • Evidence notes and unresolved questions
  • An analyst-approved decision brief

Where we can apply it

  • Market question → search-assisted draft → source review → decision brief.
  • Competitor watchlist → scheduled research → analyst triage → sales talking points.
  • Content topic → evidence collection → editor review → sourced article outline.
01

Use case 1

Prepare a source-linked competitor or category research brief.

02

Use case 2

Collect supporting material for a reviewed content outline.

03

Use case 3

Refresh a watchlist of business topics on an agreed cadence.

Inputs we need

  • A precise research question
  • Approved source or market scope
  • A dated decision-brief template

Delivery sequence

  • Set scope, date context, and required evidence before searching.
  • Gather relevant sources and preserve their links with the draft.
  • Verify important statements and label inference before stakeholder delivery.

Expert review points

  • Check the original source and publication date for material claims.
  • Avoid presenting search visibility as proof of commercial performance.

We confirm available integrations, plans, permissions, and data mapping before implementing these connection candidates.

  • n8n
  • Retool
  • Custom research applications
  • Data warehouses

Signals we can make visible

  • Source verification rate
  • Brief turnaround time
  • Research acceptance rate
  • Cost per approved brief

We agree the source, population, period, denominator, and decision behind each measure.
